locator: §5.2, 'For minimal propositions, properties, and so on will likely not be suited to do much explanatory work of the sort that robust propositions, properties, and so on are suited for.'
interpretation: Dreier's proposal (2018) for keeping the minimal/robust contrast after the collapse argument. The distinction between realism and anti-realism is drawn by the order of explanation, and robust propositions and properties are suited to explanatory work, while minimal ones 'will likely not be suited to do much' of it. Read as: if a moral sentence is robustly truth-apt, its truth conditions are suited to explain our thought and talk with it. Only suitability of robust truth conditions is attributed; the hedged remark about minimal ones is not formalized, and nothing here says minimal truth conditions cannot explain. That robust truth conditions actually explain is the separate, unattributed open premise STMT-ROBUST-MORAL-TRUTH-IS-EXPLANATORY (Codex P1 on #230); suitedToExplainDoesNotGiveBridge shows this claim does not supply it. The entry gives the proposal conditionally ('If this can be defended'), so the claim records the proposal, not its defense. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
